difficultyRationale: Requires distinguishing Spring's supported injection of a strategy collection from the explicit registration needed to build an enum-keyed dispatch map, then comparing that refactor with three alternatives.
explanation: A Strategy refactor replaces payment-type branches inside PaymentService with a lookup. Spring can inject the available PaymentStrategy beans as a List, but the service must explicitly index them by each strategy's supported PaymentType. Automatic injection of a map of beans uses String bean-name keys, not enum keys. A new type adds a PaymentType value and a strategy implementation rather than another PaymentService branch.

options.text: Replace the if/else chain with a `switch` expression over `PaymentType`, which is more concise and easier to read.
options.explanation: A `switch` expression is a readability improvement, but every new payment type still requires adding a case to this same method — it does not change the extension story at all, which is what OCP is actually asking about here.

options.text: Define a `PaymentStrategy` interface declaring `PaymentType supportedType()` and `void charge(PaymentRequest request)`, with one Spring-managed `@Component` implementation per payment type. Constructor-inject `List<PaymentStrategy>` into `PaymentService`, explicitly build a `Map<PaymentType, PaymentStrategy>` using `Collectors.toUnmodifiableMap(PaymentStrategy::supportedType, Function.identity())`, and dispatch by `request.type()`, rejecting unsupported types.
options.explanation: Correct. Spring injects all matching `PaymentStrategy` beans into the `List`. `PaymentService` then explicitly constructs its enum-keyed registry using `supportedType()`; a new payment type requires its enum value and a strategy bean, not another `PaymentService` branch. Duplicate supported types fail registry construction instead of silently overriding one another. Spring does not automatically populate a `Map<PaymentType, PaymentStrategy>`.

options.text: Add a `boolean supportsCrypto` flag to `PaymentRequest` and branch on it at the top of `charge` before the existing if/else chain.
options.explanation: This adds a special case on top of the existing special cases rather than removing the need for them; every future payment type would need its own flag and its own branch, which is the opposite direction from OCP's goal.

options.text: Make `creditCardGateway`, `payPalClient` and `bankTransferService` all implement a shared `Gateway` marker interface with no methods, purely so `PaymentService` can hold all three in a single `List<Gateway>` field and iterate over them, even though nothing about a `Gateway` reference lets `charge` determine which element in that list actually corresponds to `request.type()`.
options.explanation: A marker interface with no methods gives `PaymentService` nothing to call polymorphically, so the if/else chain (or an equivalent type check) would still be needed to decide which gateway handles the request; it adds a type without adding an extension point.
